draft.title: Conduction
card: Conduction is the way heat passes through a material from particle to particle. Hot particles vibrate more and bump into their neighbours, passing energy along.
Heat moves from the hotter part of an object to the cooler part. The material itself does not move from one place to another.
a material that lets heat pass through easily. Metals such as copper and iron are good conductors.
a material that heat passes through slowly. Air and wool are insulators, so they are used to keep heat in or out.
draft.remember: Conduction passes heat by particle collisions. Metals pass it on quickly, air and wool slowly.

a.q: Jaz leaves a metal spoon in a hot soup. Soon the handle feels warm. How did the heat reach the handle?
opts: Particles in the spoon collided and passed energy along
Hot soup particles travelled up the spoon to the handle
Warm air rose from the soup and heated the handle
The spoon's particles all moved from the bowl to the handle
a.why: Heat travelled along the metal as particles bumped into their neighbours. The particles stayed in place and only passed on energy, so the idea that soup particles climbed the spoon is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what the particles in the spoon do to their neighbours.

b.q: Lena wears a wool jumper on a cold day in Hobart and stays warm. Why does wool help?
opts: It is an insulator, so heat leaves her body slowly
It is a conductor, so heat moves through it quickly
It makes heat for her body through its fibres
It stops her body from losing any heat at all
b.why: Wool holds a lot of air, and air and wool are insulators. They slow the passing of heat from her warm body to the cold air. The last option is wrong because insulators slow heat loss and do not stop it.
b.clue: Which kind of material passes heat on slowly?

a.best: Particles in the spoon collided and passed energy along

b.best: It is an insulator, so heat leaves her body slowly

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the 'stops her body from losing any heat at all' option 'the last option'. Options are shown in random order, and here the last option is 'It is a conductor, so heat moves through it quickly'. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.
